senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; preced.) joy, rejoicing, festive occasion.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 8a:10">Keth. 8ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>אפושי ש׳ בעלמא הוא</he> it is merely an extension of the wedding joy (not a new festive occasion).

<cite ref="Ketubot 8a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>מברך שהש׳ במעונו</he> he says the benediction containing the words, ‘in whose dwelling there is joy.’ <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 9:2:2">Y. B. Bath. IX, 16ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>שִׂמְחַת זכר</he> the joy over the birth of a male child.
Gen. R. s. 70; M. Kat. 8ᵇ ש׳ בש׳, v. עָרב I; a. fr.—Esp. שמחת יום טוב, or ש׳ the rejoicing on the festival (Deut. XVI, 11; 14).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 6b:16">R. Hash. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>איתה בש׳</he> she (woman) is included in the commandment to observe the festival with joy.

<cite ref="Chagigah 6a:4">Ḥag. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>חנה … מיחייבא בש׳</he> was not Hannah herself bound to visit the Temple in order to rejoice? <cite ref="Pesachim 109a:5">Pes. 109ᵃ</cite> <he>בזמן … אין ש׳ אלא בבשר … אין ש׳ אלא ביין</he> as long as the Temple stood, the festive rejoicing consisted in eating meat (of the peace-offering), … but now … the festive celebration consists in partaking of wine; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שְׂמָחוֹת</he>.

Zeb. 102ᵃ חמש ש׳ היתה וכ׳ Elisheba had five joys (distinctions) more than ordinary daughters of Israel: her brother-in-law (Moses) was king &c.; a. e.—ש׳ (מסכת) S’maḥoth, one of the small treatises of Talmud Babli, euphem. for אבל רבתי, v. אֵבֶל.
